ehg_apparent.provenance: REAL-PINNED (public TPEHGDB features + published flaw; the pipeline is our port, not the authors' code)
ehg_apparent.source_data: PhysioNet TPEHGDB v1.0.1, doi:10.13026/C2FW2V, ODC-By 1.0 (as stated on the PhysioNet page)

published.paper: Vandewiele et al., arXiv 2001.06296 v2 (Nov 2020), Artif Intell Med 2021; code github.com/GillesVandewiele/EHG-oversampling
published.closest_published_row: [30] RF+SMOTE: 96.40 (before) vs 46.97 (after, default SMOTE) => +49.4 AUC points; vs 43.78 with no oversampling
published.note: published used 298 recordings and their own re-implemented features (many per study); this case uses the 12 PhysioNet-shipped features, so only the direction and rough size are comparable

ehg_apparent.flaw: SMOTE-style oversampling is applied to the whole data set before the cross-validation split, so synthetic copies of held-out rare-class rows (and rows next to them) are in the training folds; the control is to oversample inside each training fold only
